You can grant this permission later. Until then, CyanBridge will not be able to find, pair with, or connect to your glasses.

CyanBridge has no Accessibility service of its own. Screen Memory and the Local Agent work through Tasker and AutoInput: AutoInput\'s Accessibility service reads the text and interface structure of the app on your screen and lets the Local Agent tap, type, scroll, and navigate on your behalf. You enable AutoInput\'s Accessibility yourself; CyanBridge never turns it on. Screen content for Screen Memory is stored locally. When you ask the Local Agent to do something, the current screen content may be processed by the AI provider you selected, including a cloud provider if you chose one. Screenshots are optional and off by default. You turn them on in the CyanBridge Local Agent Tasker profile; after that, each planning screenshot goes to the planner you selected, including a cloud or Pro planner. Apps you block in Tasker are skipped. You can turn off AutoInput\'s Accessibility, Screen Memory, or the Local Agent at any time.
